items.stem: In most apps, why is code often attached to 'events' such as a button tap?

options.text: Because the app waits for the user to act, then the matching code runs in response
options.rationale: Correct: event-driven apps respond to user actions.

options.text: Because events make the phone charge faster

options.rationale: Apps commonly use buttons tied to events.

options.text: Because code can only ever run once
options.rationale: Event code can run many times, each time the event happens.

items.explanation: Correct: event-driven apps respond to user actions.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when designing an app's interface? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Making the main action clear and easy to find
options.rationale: Correct: a clear main action improves usability.

options.text: Testing the layout with real users
options.rationale: Correct: user testing reveals confusing design.

options.text: Packing every screen with as many buttons as possible
options.rationale: Cluttered screens are harder to use.

options.text: Hiding how to move between screens
options.rationale: Users need a clear flow between screens.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear main action improves usability.

items.stem: After testing, a user keeps tapping the wrong button to add an item. What is the best response?

options.text: Improve the design (clearer label or placement) and test again
options.rationale: Correct: iterate on the design based on user feedback.

options.text: Blame the user for tapping wrongly
options.rationale: Design should guide users, not blame them.
